purpose: Nadolol is used to treat high blood pressure and chest pain (angina). Lowering high blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It can also help reduce how often you get chest pain.
how_it_works: Your heart has tiny receptors that respond to stress hormones like adrenaline. Nadolol blocks those receptors, which slows your heart rate down and reduces the force your heart pumps with. This takes pressure off your heart and lowers your blood pressure.
common_side_effects: Feeling tired or sluggish, slow heartbeat, dizziness, cold hands or feet, upset stomach, and shortness of breath with exercise. Some people also feel a little lightheaded when they stand up quickly.
warnings: Never stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor — stopping abruptly can cause serious heart problems, including chest pain or a heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have asthma, diabetes, or breathing problems, as this medicine can make those conditions worse. It can also mask the fast heartbeat that warns you of low blood sugar if you are diabetic.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 40 mg taken once a day by mouth. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose as needed, typically up to 80–320 mg per day depending on your condition. Since it is taken only once a day, try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
